review_type: Source-grounded AI review; the reviewer authored these development fixtures and knew expected labels. This is not independent human calibration.
conclusion: Both positive answers were accepted. The init completeness defect was missed; the overview negative was rejected for different, partly debatable reasons. The 3/4 label match does not establish that either targeted semantic defect was repaired.

issues: The connection paragraph puts S9 ('score production traffic with the same scorers you use in evaluation') next to Signals, which suggests that Agents-view Signals reuse your evaluation scorers. S9 is from the 'Monitor production' section and links to the guardrails/monitors guide. None of the evidence read shows that Agents-view Signals use evaluation scorers. S1 only says they score with an LLM judge or with a remote scorer endpoint that you host. Either say that S9 is about production monitors/guardrails rather than Agents-view Signals, or remove the implied link.

The answer frames evaluations strictly as 'testing before release' or 'before you ship'. The sources describe repeatable test cases, comparing changes over time and spotting regressions. S6 says evaluations are also used to 'benchmark and monitor'. Soften the pre-release-only framing.

cases.semantic_assessment: The requested negative label was returned, but neither reported issue identifies whole-conversation scoring versus turn scoring. This is not evidence that the operational-target defect was repaired.

issue_assessment.assessment: Plausible ambiguity warning: S9 links to legacy guardrails/monitors; placing its reusable-scorer statement next to Agents-view Signals can imply an unproven integration. The candidate does not explicitly assert that integration, so this is stronger than an established falsehood.

Overreach in reading exclusivity: the candidate describes a before-release use case but does not say evaluations can only run before release. S6 supports monitoring as another use. Broadening the framing improves it; this alone is not a material unsupported claim.

cases.paired_consistency: Both warned-about passages are unchanged in the minimally corrected positive, which was accepted. A single stochastic call per candidate cannot establish the reason for the different label.

cases.semantic_assessment: Accepted the minimally corrected answer; agent turns are now the scoring target. Source S1 supports that distinction. Other monitor/evaluation framing is unchanged, so the pair does not show stable treatment of the negative verdict reasons.

Naming OpenTelemetry jargon is less important than describing those effects.
